review.translation: [I will|1] [also|0] [put|1] [hostility|0] [between you|2] [and|3] [the woman|4], [and between|5] [your offspring|6] [and|7] [her offspring|8]. [He|9] [will strike you|10] [{on} the head|11], [and you|12] [will strike him|13] [{on} the heel|14].”

analysis.evidence: אֵיבָה is the object of אָשִׁית, “I will put.” The paired בֵּין phrases identify the parties to this hostility, first the serpent and the woman, then their respective offspring. The blows to head and heel illustrate the enmity.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: the enmity God sets between the serpent and the woman

analysis.evidence: אֵיבָה “enmity” precedes אָשִׁית as its direct object. The paired בֵּין phrases specify where the speaker will put that enmity, first between the serpent and the woman and then between their offspring.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular, with the preformative א and no suffix.
analysis.sense: to put or set something between parties

analysis.evidence: In וְאֵיבָה אָשִׁית בֵּינְךָ וּבֵין הָאִשָּׁה, “I will put enmity between you and the woman,” the suffix identifies the serpent as one party to the enmity, and וּבֵין הָאִשָּׁה identifies the woman as the other.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with a second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix referring to the serpent.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In בֵּינְךָ וּבֵין הָאִשָּׁה ‘between you and the woman’, וּבֵין introduces the woman as the second party to the enmity (אֵיבָה) that God sets between her and the serpent.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ ‘and’ prefixed to the preposition בֵּין, with no suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: בֵּינְךָ וּבֵין הָאִשָּׁה means “between you and the woman.” The parallel phrase contrasts the serpent’s offspring with זַרְעָהּ, “her offspring,” referring back to the woman.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ.

analysis.evidence: In וּבֵין זַרְעֲךָ וּבֵין זַרְעָהּ, the marked וּבֵין introduces “your offspring” as the first of two parties. The next וּבֵין introduces “her offspring” as the other. אֵיבָה אָשִׁית (“I will put enmity”) identifies the relationship between them.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בֵּין with prefixed conjunction וּ and no suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: The suffix ־ךָ refers to the serpent. The parallel phrases וּבֵין זַרְעֲךָ וּבֵין זַרְעָהּ extend the enmity between the serpent and the woman to their respective offspring.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with the second-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ךָ.

analysis.evidence: In וּבֵין זַרְעֲךָ וּבֵין זַרְעָהּ, “and between your offspring and hers,” the marked וּבֵין introduces her offspring as the second party to the enmity expressed by וְאֵיבָה אָשִׁית.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ prefixed to the preposition בֵּין, with no suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs the serpent and the woman, then extends their enmity to זַרְעֲךָ ‘your offspring’ and זַרְעָהּ ‘her offspring’. The suffix ־ָהּ refers to הָאִשָּׁה ‘the woman’.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person feminine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to זַרְעָהּ (“her offspring”). It agrees with the masculine singular noun זֶרַע and marks the subject of יְשׁוּפְךָ (“he will strike you”), in contrast with וְאַתָּה (“and you”) in the next clause.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person masculine singular.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew verb entry for שׁוּף with the Qal sense ‘strike’.
draft.definition: To strike an opponent, here on the head.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:15 the woman's offspring strikes the serpent on the head, and the serpent in turn strikes the offspring on the heel. The repeated verb describes the hostile action common to both clauses.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to זַרְעָהּ, the woman's offspring. The suffix ־ךָ identifies the serpent as the one struck, and רֹאשׁ specifies where the blow lands. The next clause reverses the participants and uses the same verb with עָקֵב, the heel.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third masculine singular, with a second masculine singular direct-object suffix ־ךָ.
analysis.sense: To strike an opponent on a particular part of the body.

analysis.evidence: In יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ, the suffix ךָ identifies the serpent as the one struck, and רֹאשׁ specifies where the blow lands. The parallel עָקֵב ‘heel’ names the body part struck in return.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The explicit אַתָּה contrasts the serpent with הוּא, the woman’s offspring, in the preceding clause. The verb תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ already marks a second-person masculine singular subject, so the pronoun highlights the serpent’s part in the reciprocal action.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the independent second-person masculine singular pronoun אַתָּה.
analysis.sense: you, as for you (the one addressed set apart)

draft.change: Add שׁוּף with the transitive Qal sense “strike.”
draft.definition: Strike an opponent on a particular part of the body.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:15 the serpent strikes the heel of the one who strikes its head. The repeated verb expresses the action shared by both clauses.

analysis.evidence: וְאַתָּה identifies the serpent as the subject. The suffix ־ֶנּוּ refers to the woman’s offspring, and עָקֵב locates the strike at his heel. The preceding clause uses the same verb with the roles reversed and רֹאשׁ, “head,” as the point of impact. Both clauses describe one party striking the other.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second masculine singular (תְּ־), with third masculine singular direct-object suffix (־ֶנּוּ).
analysis.sense: Strike an opponent on a particular part of the body.

analysis.evidence: In תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב, the suffix on the verb identifies whom the serpent strikes, and עָקֵב specifies where the blow lands. It parallels רֹאשׁ (“head”) in the preceding clause.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun without prefix or suffix.
